research_question: Do customers with previous returns have a different subsequent return rate compared with customers without previous returns?
null_hypothesis: H0: p_A = p_B (equal subsequent return probabilities)
group_a_definition: Orders with at least one previous return by the same customer (point-in-time)
group_b_definition: Orders with zero previous returns by the same customer (includes first orders)
outcome: Whether the current order was returned
interpretation: At alpha = 0.05 we do not reject the null hypothesis (p = 0.5887). The observed difference in subsequent return rates is compatible with chance variation under equal population proportions. This does not prove the rates are equal, and it does not establish causation.
causation_disclaimer: Statistical significance describes evidence against equal proportions. It does not imply that prior returns cause later returns.
